354706.title: Egerváry decomposition characterization and independence-number conjecture
354706.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with a perfect matching and a Deming decomposition

$$
\{\{ B_i\}_{i=1}^r, \{ K_j\}_{j=1}^{\ell},R\}.
$$

A Deming-$K_4$ subgraph is denoted by $K_j$, the residual subgraph by $R$, and $M_R$ is the matching induced by restricting the relevant perfect matching to $R$. **Egerváry decomposition characterization conjecture.** The graph $G$ is Egerváry if and only if: there are no Deming-BP subgraphs; each Deming-$K_4$ subgraph $K_j$ is Egerváry; every edge in each $K_j$ is in a perfect matching of $G$; the Deming-$K_4$ subgraphs are independent; each graph $K_j+R$ is Egerváry; and there are no $M_R$-alternating paths between vertices from different Deming-$K_4$ subgraphs. The conjecture proposes that the necessary conditions proved in the paper are also sufficient, thereby characterizing Egerváry graphs. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source material.

357416.title: Large-degree conjecture for multipartite hypergraphs with a heavy edge
357416.statement:
Let $r\geq 4$ and let $H$ be an $r$-partite $r$-uniform multi-hypergraph with $n$ edges. Let $\nu:=\nu_{2}(H)$ denote its matching parameter.

**Large-degree conjecture.** There exists $d_r>0$ such that if $H$ has an edge of multiplicity at least $\nu+1$, then

$$
\Delta(H)\geq \frac{n}{r-1}-d_r\nu.
$$

This statement is proposed as the generalization needed to extend the preceding results to the case $k=2$ and $r\geq 4$. The source presents it as an unresolved sufficient step for the corresponding problem.

358858.title: Weighted rainbow clique conjecture
358858.statement:
Let $r\ge 3$, $k\ge\binom{r}{2}$, and let $G_0\cong K_n$ be a complete graph on $[n]$. A **$k$-weighted graph** is a pair $\mathcal{G}=(G_0,f)$ with an edge-weighting $f$. A weight sequence bound $(1,2,\ldots,\binom{r}{2})$ means that every $K_r$ has its nondecreasing edge-weight sequence lexicographically at least this sequence. Define

$$
k_2=\left\lceil\frac{\left(\binom{r}{2}-1\right)\binom{n}{2}}{t_{r-1}(n)}\right\rceil,\qquad k_1=k_2-1.
$$

**Weighted rainbow clique conjecture.** If $n\ge r$, $G_0$ contains no $K_r$ with weight sequence bound $(1,2,\ldots,\binom{r}{2})$, then: (i) if $k=k_1$, $f(G_0)\le(\binom{r}{2}-1)\binom{n}{2}$; and (ii) if $k=k_2$, $f(G_0)\le k\,t_{r-1}(n)$.

This weighted statement is introduced as a conjectural reformulation implying the rainbow Turán clique bound. The source proves it for $r=4,5$; the general case remains open.

359651.title: Gowers's intersection conjecture for approximate quadratic varieties
359651.statement:
Let $p\geq 3$ be prime, let $G$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_p$, and let $V\subseteq G$ be a $(c_0,\delta,\varepsilon)$-approximate quadratic variety, meaning that $|V|=\delta|G|$, $\|\mathbbm{1}_V-\delta\|_{\mathsf{U}^2}\leq\varepsilon$, and

$$
\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{x,a,b,c} \Delta_{a,b,c}\mathbbm{1}_V(x)=c_0\delta^7.
$$

**Gowers's conjecture.** If $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small in terms of $\delta$ and $c_0$, then there exists a quadratic variety $Q$ such that

$$
|Q|\leq O_{c_0}(|V|)\quad\text{and}\quad |Q\cap V|\geq\Omega_{c_0}(|V|).
$$

The conjecture predicts that an approximate quadratic variety has substantial overlap with an exact quadratic variety of comparable size. It is presented as an open conjecture, with the resemblance to the Balog--Szemerédi--Gowers/Freiman phenomenon offered as motivation.

359935.title: Finite forbidden-subdiagram characterization of ranked Kohnert posets
359935.statement:
A **diagram** $D_0$ determines a Kohnert poset $
P(D_0)$, and $KD(D_0)$ denotes the collection of diagrams associated with $D_0$. A diagram $D$ **contains** a subdiagram from a family of subdiagrams $
F$ when at least one member of $
F$ occurs as a subdiagram of $D$.

**Finite forbidden-subdiagram conjecture.** There exists a finite number of special families of subdiagrams $\mathcal{F}$ such that, for any diagram $D_0$, $\mathcal{P}(D_0)$ is ranked if and only if there is no $D\in KD(D_0)$ such that $D$ contains a subdiagram from $\mathcal{F}$.

This conjecture proposes a finite forbidden-subdiagram characterization of rankedness for Kohnert posets. The article establishes necessary conditions and rankedness results for several special families, but a general sufficient characterization remains open.

362060.title: Conjecture on planar 2-edge-apex graphs and flexible rigidity circuits
362060.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $e$ and $f$ be edges added to $G$. A graph is **$(3,6)$-tight** if it has $3|V|-6$ edges and every subgraph $H$ with at least three vertices satisfies $|E(H)|\leq 3|V(H)|-6$; an **$\mathcal{R}_3$-circuit** is a circuit in the three-dimensional rigidity matroid, and it is **flexible** or **rigid** according as its generic rigidity rank is deficient or full. The **2-sum** of two graphs is their matroidal 2-sum along a common edge. The following hold. (i) If $G$ is planar and $G+\{e,f\}$ is a $(3,6)$-tight flexible $\mathcal{R}_3$-circuit, then $G$ is the 2-sum of two rigid $\mathcal{R}_3$-circuits. (ii) If $G$ is planar and $G+\{e,f\}$ is a flexible $\mathcal{R}_3$-circuit, then $G+\{e,f\}$ is $(3,6)$-tight. This conjecture is intended to characterize which 2-edge-apex $(3,6)$-sparse graphs are $\mathcal{R}_3$-independent; the provided text gives no resolution of either assertion.

362299.title: Polynomial Rödl property for graphs close to a proper hereditary family
362299.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of graphs. A graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is **$\alpha$-close** to $\mathcal{F}$ if one can add or delete at most $\alpha n^2/2$ edges from $G$ to obtain a graph in $\mathcal{F}$. A hereditary family is one closed under taking induced subgraphs, and it is **proper** if it is not the family of all graphs.

**Conjecture on hereditary families close to $\mathcal{F}$.** For each proper hereditary family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs there are $C_{\mathcal{F}},d_{\mathcal{F}}>0$ such that if $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, every graph on $n$ vertices which is $\varepsilon^{d_{\mathcal{F}}}$-close to $\mathcal{F}$ contains an $\varepsilon$-homogeneous set of size at least $\varepsilon^{C_{\mathcal{F}}}n$.

This conjecture extends the polynomial Rödl phenomenon from hereditary families themselves to graphs that are polynomially close to such a family. The source calls it a natural conjecture for hereditary families and provides no resolution, so its general status remains open.

363761.title: Characterization of factors guaranteeing well-dominated strong products
363761.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be nontrivial graphs. A graph is **trivially well-dominated** if its closed neighborhoods form a clique partition of its vertex set. A graph is **well-dominated** if all its minimal dominating sets have the same cardinality. The strong product $G\boxtimes H$ has vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$, with $(u_1,v_1)$ adjacent to $(u_2,v_2)$ exactly when $u_2\in N_G[u_1]$ and $v_2\in N_H[v_1]$. The graphs $G$ and $H$ are its factors.

**Characterization conjecture.** If $G$ is a well-dominated graph that is not trivially well-dominated, then there exists a well-dominated graph $H$ such that $G\boxtimes H$ is not well-dominated.

The preceding theorem shows that a trivially well-dominated factor guarantees that the strong product with every well-dominated graph is well-dominated. This conjecture asserts that these are precisely the factors with that universal property.

364157.title: DMS's conjecture on intervals of irredundant base cardinalities for primitive groups
364157.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite permutation group acting on a domain $\Omega$. An **irredundant base** is an ordered sequence $(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_\ell)$ whose associated stabilizer chain

$$
G\ge G_{\omega_1}\ge G_{\omega_1,\omega_2}\ge \cdots \ge G_{\omega_1,\omega_2,\ldots,\omega_\ell}=1
$$

has all inclusions strict, and define

$$
\mathcal{I}(G,\Omega)=\{\ell\in\mathbb{N}\mid \text{there exists an irredundant base of length }\ell\}.
$$

**DMS's conjecture.** There exists an interval $X$ of positive integers, not containing $1$, such that no primitive group $G$ acting on any domain $\Omega$ satisfies

$$
\mathcal{I}(G,\Omega)=X.
$$

Cameron proved that $\mathcal{I}(G,\Omega)$ is always an interval, while previous work established that every interval of natural numbers not containing $1$ can be realized by a finite transitive permutation group. The conjecture asserts that at least one such interval is impossible for primitive groups, distinguishing the primitive case from the transitive imprimitive constructions.

365232.title: Pardey–Rautenbach conjecture on almost colour-balanced perfect matchings
365232.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be positive integers, let $K_{2kn}$ be the complete graph on $2kn$ vertices, and let $[k]=\{1,2,\dotsc,k\}$. A colouring $c\colon E(K_{2kn})\to [k]$ is **colour-balanced** when every colour is used on the same number of edges. For a perfect matching $M$ of $K_{2kn}$, define

$$
f(M)\coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^k\left|\left|c^{-1}(i)\cap M\right|-n\right|.
$$

**Pardey–Rautenbach conjecture.** If $c\colon E(K_{2kn})\to [k]$ is colour-balanced, then there is a perfect matching $M$ of $K_{2kn}$ such that

$$
f(M)\leq \mathcal{O}(k^2).
$$

The conjecture seeks a bound depending only on the number of colours, rather than on the number of vertices. Pardey and Rautenbach proposed it after showing that an exactly colour-balanced perfect matching need not exist for three colours; the paper improves the previous bound, which depended on $n$, to an explicit bound of $4^{k^2}$, but does not establish the conjectured quadratic dependence.

365712.title: The iSWAP optimality conjecture for 2-local unitary circuit ensembles
365712.statement:
Let $n\geq 3$, let $\mathcal{G}$ be a fixed connected graph, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be a 2-local unitary circuit ensemble. Write $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}_{2,\mathcal{G}}^{\mathcal{E}}$ for its associated second-moment operator and $\Delta(\cdot)$ for the convergence gap. Assume that $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}_{2,\mathcal{G}}^{\mathcal{E}}$ is Hermitian. **The iSWAP optimality conjecture.**

$$
\Delta\!\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}_{2,\mathcal{G}}^{\mathcal{E}}\right)\leq \Delta\!\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}_{2,\mathcal{G}}^{\operatorname{\mathsf{iSWAP}}}\right).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the iSWAP gadget gives at least as large a convergence gap as every admissible 2-local circuit ensemble on every connected interaction graph, supporting its optimality in forming unitary 2-designs. The paper states that this claim has not been fully resolved.

366393.title: The almost Pieri coloring conjecture
366393.statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\widetilde{\alpha}$ be as in the almost Pieri rule: $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r)\vdash n$ with $\alpha_r>1$, $r\geq1$, $k$ is positive, and $\widetilde{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r,1^k)$. Let $\mu\vdash n$ have an admissible tableau $Q\in\operatorname{SYT}(\mu)$ such that $Q^\uparrow$ admits an $\alpha$-coloring. Suppose that $\lambda$ is obtained from $\mu$ by the box-addition procedure in the almost Pieri rule.

**Almost Pieri coloring conjecture.** There exists an admissible $\widetilde{Q}\in\operatorname{SYT}(\lambda)$ such that $\widetilde{Q}^\uparrow$ admits a $\widetilde{\alpha}$-coloring.

This is the coloring formulation of the almost Pieri phenomenon: adding fixed points should extend an existing admissible coloring after the prescribed additions of boxes. It is presented as a conjecture and remains open.

367172.title: The Orlik–Terao conjecture for graphical configuration spaces
367172.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a directed graph, let $X(SU(2),\Gamma)$ be its graphical configuration space, and let $\overline{\operatorname{OT}}(\Gamma)$ be the reduced Orlik–Terao algebra associated with its graphical vector arrangement. Let $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$ be the automorphism group of the underlying undirected graph, acting on both the cohomology and the reduced Orlik–Terao algebra. **Orlik–Terao conjecture.** For any graph $\Gamma$, there exists a degree-halving isomorphism of graded $\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$-representations

$$
H^*(X(SU(2),\Gamma);\mathbb{Q})\cong\overline{\operatorname{OT}}(\Gamma).
$$

This conjecture predicts that the cohomology representation of the graphical configuration space is encoded by the reduced Orlik–Terao algebra. The supplied source gives no evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

367211.title: Conjectured description of the second half of the connective KO-theory summands
367211.statement:
Let $k$ be an index for the spectra $\mathcal{A}_k$, let $\mathcal{E}_{i,k}$ denote the $i$th edge of $\mathcal{Sigma}^{-2^{k+1}}\mathcal{A}_k$, and let $M_i$, $y_1$, and $z_j$ denote the summands and classes used in the decomposition. For exponents $varepsilon_j\in\{0,1\}$, set

$$
S=\sum \varepsilon_j.
$$

The exponent $t$ is defined by

$$
t=2^{k-2}-2-2^{i-3}-\sum 2^{j-1}\varepsilon_j,
$$

and set

$$
D=2^i+4t+8+\sum 2^{j+2}\varepsilon_j.
$$

**Conjectured second-half description.** The $\nu$ summands in the second half of $\mathcal{A}_k$ are $y_1^{2^{k-2}-2}M_{k+1}$ and all

$$
y_1^t z_3^{\varepsilon_3}\cdots z_{k-2}^{\varepsilon_{k-2}}z_{k-1}M_i
$$

with $4\le i\le k$, $\varepsilon_j\in\{0,1\}$, $\varepsilon_j=0$ if $j<i-1$, and $t=2^{k-2}-2-2^{i-3}-\sum 2^{j-1}\varepsilon_j$. Their corresponding edges are

$$
y_1^{2^{k-2}-2}M_{k+1}\leftrightarrow \Sigma^{2^k}\mathcal{E}_{2,k}
$$

and

$$
y_1^t z_3^{\varepsilon_3}\cdots z_{k-2}^{\varepsilon_{k-2}}z_{k-1}M_i\leftrightarrow \Sigma^D\mathcal{E}_{S+3,i+S}.
$$

These constitute exactly the second half of $\Sigma^{-2^{k+1}}\mathcal{A}_k$.

368246.title: Pancyclicity conjecture for Bang–Jensen–Gutin–Li type conditions
368246.statement: A digraph $D$ has order $n\ge 3$. A pair of nonadjacent vertices is **dominated** if it has a common in-neighbor, and **dominating** if it has a common out-neighbor. Let $d(u)$ denote the total degree of a vertex $u$, and let $\mathcal{D}_L$ be the class of non-pancyclic locally semicomplete digraphs defined by the stated round-decomposition characterization. Let $\mathcal{D}_B$ be the class of balanced complete bipartite digraphs with at least $4$ vertices. **Pancyclicity conjecture.** If every vertex $u\in V(D)$ belonging to a nonadjacent dominated pair or a nonadjacent dominating pair satisfies $d(u)\ge n$, then $D$ is pancyclic unless $D\in\mathcal{D}_L$ or $D\in\mathcal{D}_B$. This conjecture seeks a pancyclicity criterion extending Bang–Jensen–Gutin–Li type Hamiltonicity conditions; the exceptional classes account for known non-pancyclic structures, while a complete characterization of non-pancyclic locally semicomplete digraphs under the relevant condition remains difficult.

369903.title: The $T^{**}(r,n)$ extremal stability conjecture
369903.statement:
Let $k,r,b$ be integers with $k\geq 2$, $r=2k+b$, and $3\leq b\leq 2k$. Let $T^{**}(r,n)$ be the three-block graph consisting of a complete bipartite block with parts of sizes $\left\lfloor\frac{n-r+2}{2}\right\rfloor$ and $\left\lceil\frac{n-r+2}{2}\right\rceil$, together with blocks $K_{2k}$ and $K_b$. **$T^{**}(r,n)$ extremal stability conjecture.** There exists an integer $n_0$ such that every $C_{2k+1}$-free graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with $n\geq n_0$ and 
$$
e(G)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{(n-r+2)^2}{4}\right\rfloor+\binom{2k}{2}+\binom{b}{2}
$$
 satisfies 
$$
\gamma_2(G)\leq 2\binom{k}{2}+\binom{\left\lfloor\frac b2\right\rfloor}{2}+\binom{\left\lceil\frac b2\right\rceil}{2},
$$
 and equality holds if and only if $G=T^{**}(r,n)$. This is the formal version of the preceding next-stability claim and is intended to identify the unique equality case for the stated edge threshold.

370158.title: The induced double-wheel conjecture for $K_{1,d}$-free graphs
370158.statement:
Let $k,d$ be positive integers. The Cartesian product $G\openbox H$ is the graph with vertex set $V(G)\times V(H)$ in which $(u_1,v_1)$ and $(u_2,v_2)$ are adjacent exactly when either $u_1=u_2$ and $v_1v_2\in E(H)$, or $v_1=v_2$ and $u_1u_2\in E(G)$. A **$k$-double wheel** is $C\openbox P_2$, where $C$ is a cycle on $k$ vertices. A graph is $K_{1,d}$-free if it has no induced $K_{1,d}$, and $\operatorname{\alpha\text{-}\mathsf{tw}}(G)$ denotes its tree-independence number.

**Double-wheel conjecture.** There exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}^2\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that every $K_{1,d}$-free graph $G$ with $\operatorname{\alpha\text{-}\mathsf{tw}}(G)\geq f(k,d)$ contains the $k$-double wheel as an induced minor.

The double wheel is proposed as an intermediate structure toward a cylindrical induced grid, obtained by closing a ladder into a cycle. The paper notes that proving the conjecture would require new methods, and its status remains open.

372835.title: Conjecture on bichromatic triangles or quadrangles around a blue polygon
372835.statement:
Consider a bicolored pseudoline arrangement, with pseudolines colored blue or red. Let $P$ be a blue $k$-gon, meaning a polygonal face or region bounded by blue pseudolines, and suppose that at least $k-4$ red pseudolines pass through $P$. A **bichromatic triangle or quadrangle on the inside boundary** is a triangular or quadrilateral face incident with the inside boundary of $P$ and supported by pseudolines of both colors.

**Blue-polygon bichromatic-face conjecture.** Given a blue $k$-gon $P$ with at least $k-4$ red pseudolines passing through, there exists a bichromatic triangle or quadrangle on its inside boundary.

The authors introduce this as an intermediate statement toward proving that every non-trivially bicolored arrangement contains a bichromatic triangle or quadrangle. They report that they could not prove it; its general status is open.

373112.title: Finiteness conjecture for symmetric abstract 2-rigidity matroids
373112.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\mathcal{R}_n$ denote the $2$-rigidity matroid on the edge set of the complete graph on $[n]$, and let $K_{3,3}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of size three. A matroid on this edge set is **symmetric** if it is invariant under relabelling the vertices, and it is an **abstract $2$-rigidity matroid** if it has the relevant $2$-rigidity rank properties.

**Finiteness conjecture.** There are only finitely many values of $n$ for which there exists a symmetric abstract $2$-rigidity matroid $\mathcal{M}_n\neq\mathcal{R}_n$ in which $K_{3,3}$ is independent.

The conjecture asks whether the exceptional distinction between symmetric $2$-rigidity matroids and the standard $2$-rigidity matroid can occur for arbitrarily large numbers of vertices. The paper gives an example at $n=6$ and reports no further examples at $n=7$, but does not resolve the question in general.

374800.title: The bubble-tree blow-up and comparison conjecture for KSBA moduli
374800.statement:
Let $M_N$ be the KSBA moduli stack of index one covers, let $M_N^{\operatorname{Bub}}$ be the moduli stack of bubble-tree index one cover DM stacks, and let $M_N^{\operatorname{lci}}$ be the moduli stack of lci covers. The relevant locus in $M_N$ is the locus whose corresponding surfaces contain bad simple elliptic or cusp singularities with embedded dimension at least $6$. **Bubble-tree blow-up and comparison conjecture.** The moduli stack $M_N^{\operatorname{Bub}}$ can be obtained from $M_N$ by finitely many blow-ups along this locus. Moreover, there is a birational morphism

$$
M_N^{\operatorname{Bub}}\dashrightarrow M_N^{\operatorname{lci}}
$$

for which both stacks admit contraction morphisms to $M_N$.

This conjecture predicts that the bubble-tree compactification is birationally related to the lci-cover compactification and is obtained from the KSBA space by resolving the specified singularity locus. Its status is not established in the supplied text.
